players.product: quartz / ceramic / CVD-SiC chamber parts, vacuum feedthroughs and parts cleaning

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (annual securities report): net sales JPY 288,933 million (+5.3%), operating income JPY 27,561 million (+14.4%), ordinary income JPY 26,063 million (+2.0%), profit attributable to owners of the parent JPY 14,886 million (-5.1%). Segments: Semiconductor Equipment-Related net sales JPY 185,139 million (+12.0%), operating income JPY 16,048 million (+30.4%); Electronic Devices net sales JPY 57,584 million (+14.1%), operating income JPY 10,465 million (+26.9%); Automotive-Related net sales JPY 29,245 million (-4.0%), operating income JPY 2,694 million (-25.1%); Other net sales JPY 16,964 million (-39.8%), operating loss JPY 297 million. Sales by location: Japan JPY 39,703 million, China JPY 161,289 million, US JPY 67,875 million, other JPY 20,064 million.
quarterly_data.figure: FY net sales JPY 288,933 million (+5.3%); operating income JPY 27,561 million (+14.4%); Semiconductor Equipment-Related sales JPY 185,139 million (+12.0%)

quarterly_data.signal: Management states that, as demand for semiconductors and semiconductor manufacturing equipment grew, vacuum seals, metal-processed products for manufacturing equipment and ceramics posted sharply higher sales, helped by increased orders from US and Chinese makers; quartz products and parts-cleaning services used in semiconductor processes also grew on recovering fab utilization. CVD-SiC products saw slightly lower sales because the start-up of the China factory ran into difficulties, and quartz crucibles declined as shipments to solar panel makers were curbed. Operating income rose on higher factory utilization, improved profit at new factories and a better product mix.

Thermoelectric (thermo) modules: management states that sales to optical transceiver makers rose on heavy generative-AI server investment, with demand staying at a high level and contributing substantially to profit. The company's micro modules are adopted for thermal management inside optical transceivers essential for high-volume data transmission, an area it will focus on; it opened a new lab in Yokohama to strengthen development and evaluation of 'total thermal solutions', and is developing thermistor elements for optical communications and power semiconductors, where customer demand is increasing.

Orders and production for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (annual securities report, at selling prices): total orders received JPY 260,912 million (104.6% of the prior year) and order backlog JPY 34,772 million (116.9%); Semiconductor Equipment-Related orders JPY 188,733 million (113.2%) with backlog JPY 17,636 million (125.6%). Total production JPY 299,847 million (107.7%), of which Semiconductor Equipment-Related JPY 194,311 million (114.7%).
quarterly_data.figure: order backlog JPY 34,772 million (116.9% YoY); Semiconductor Equipment-Related backlog JPY 17,636 million (125.6%)

quarterly_data.signal: Capex in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 totalled JPY 54,598 million, mainly purchases of production equipment at Chinese subsidiaries. The capex plan (new / expanded facilities) for the next fiscal year - the year ending December 2026, after a planned change of fiscal year-end from March to December - is JPY 65,000 million: Semiconductor Equipment-Related JPY 46,000 million (capacity increases for metal-processed products, quartz, ceramics, silicon parts, parts cleaning, etc.), Electronic Devices and Automotive-Related JPY 17,000 million (capacity increases for power semiconductor substrates, thermo modules and sensors), Other JPY 2,000 million.
quarterly_data.figure: FY capex JPY 54,598 million; next-year capex plan JPY 65,000 million (Semiconductor Equipment-Related JPY 46,000 million)

quarterly_data.signal: Management's priorities: further strengthen the China mass-production bases to capture strong domestic Chinese demand while, in line with customers' regional strategies, setting up and smoothly ramping mass-production bases in Malaysia and Japan; specifically, get production on track at the Kulim Plant 2 in Kedah, northern Malaysia, which starts operation in 2026, to meet customers' procurement needs, and proceed with factory construction in Beijing, Hefei, Shaoxing and Wuhan, China.
quarterly_data.figure: Kulim Plant 2 (Kedah, Malaysia) starts operation in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Results against plan and outlook (annual securities report): the fiscal year ended March 2026 delivered net sales JPY 2,889 oku against a plan of JPY 2,850 oku, operating income JPY 275 oku (plan JPY 280 oku) and net income JPY 148 oku (plan JPY 160 oku). The forecast for the fiscal year ending December 2026 (a planned nine-month transition period for the parent, subject to shareholder approval of the fiscal year-end change) is net sales JPY 3,500 oku, operating income JPY 380 oku (10.9% margin) and net income attributable to owners of the parent JPY 230 oku; the mid-term plan sets FY ending December 2027 at net sales JPY 4,000 oku, operating income JPY 480 oku and net income JPY 300 oku. Long-term targets: ROE 15%, ROIC 8%, equity ratio 40%.
quarterly_data.figure: FY12/2026 forecast: net sales JPY 3,500 oku, operating income JPY 380 oku, net income JPY 230 oku; FY12/2027 plan: net sales JPY 4,000 oku

quarterly_data.signal: Management states that in the electronics industry, generative-AI investment remains strong and a further increase in demand for semiconductor manufacturing equipment is expected, driven by memory prices rising since the second half of the year; meanwhile the power semiconductor market continues to see an adjustment in EV demand, and in Automotive-Related the AMB substrate selling-price decline from mid-year weighed on profit.

R&D (annual securities report; R&D expenses JPY 12,430 million): in vacuum seals the company is working on multiple ferrofluid-seal development projects for new and improved models of major semiconductor equipment makers; in fine and machinable ceramics it is developing high-performance parts for leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing and inspection equipment, with inquiries from major domestic and overseas customers and sample shipments and in-tool evaluation of new products progressing; in CVD-SiC, multiple in-tool evaluations of prototypes using new technology are under way.

Wafer capacity (R&D section of the annual securities report): at Lishui, China, the company built its second plant - an integrated 12-inch plant from ingot to wafer processing - and is installing equipment for the phase 1 plan of 15 ten-thousand wafers per month; the plant started operation and mass production this year. An epitaxial-wafer plant in Lishui is in mass production. In reclaimed wafers, an expansion of the Tongling plant is planned, with the aim of reaching mass production of 30 ten-thousand wafers per month from this fiscal year onward, and a new plant is being built in the Hefei area, targeting operation next fiscal year.
quarterly_data.figure: Lishui Plant 2 phase 1: 15 ten-thousand 12-inch wafers per month; Tongling reclaimed wafers: 30 ten-thousand per month target
